I've seen some pretty weird bugs seemingly popping up out of nowhere in code I wrote myself. One of the strangest was in a game I wrote, every now and then an enemy would spontaneously combust (they should only explode when shot though), and sometimes when that happened the game would freeze. It was a rare event, so the debugger wouldn't offer much help sorting it out. What really surprised me was that the game didn't really freeze up, it paused Itself! I inspected the code and confirmed that the only time the pause function was mentioned in it was when the pause button was pressed, so that bug should have been impossible. Eventually I found out that I made a mistake in the collision detection. I was testing for collisions with more things than there really were, and it just happened to interpret the pause button as the kill switch in some rare cases.

The point is, even in a completely controlled situation, mundane factors can conspire to yield mysterious and baffling results. Had I not known better, I'd have thought Gremlins were screwing around in my computer.
